name: rankwant

scripts.typecheck: npm run typecheck --workspace @rankwant/shared && npm run typecheck --workspace rankwant-web
scripts.test: npm run test --workspace @rankwant/shared && npm run test --workspace rankwant-web

#optionalDependencies: ⚠️ These are the LINUX native binaries of the toolchain packages we use.
They are listed explicitly because npm has a long-standing bug: a package
whose own `optionalDependencies` carry `os`/`cpu` constraints gets those
entries DROPPED from `packages{}` when the lockfile is generated on another
platform (npm/cli#4828, #8320). This repo's lockfile is generated on Windows
and consumed on Linux CI, so `npm ci` installed only the win32 binaries and
every native consumer died at runtime — measured 2026-09-24:
ship this way. Declaring the Linux variant as a first-class optional
dependency makes npm record it in the lockfile, so `npm ci` installs it.
The win32 variants come along automatically through the packages' own
optionalDependencies; only this side of the divide needs the nudge.
#overrides: npm reads `overrides` only from the workspace ROOT; the block in apps/web/package.json
was silently ignored (measured 2026-10-08: monaco-editor pins dompurify 3.4.15 exactly,
rehype-katex and micromark-extension-math each carried their own katex 0.16.47, and
katex: one copy, the version apps/web depends on, so the rendered HTML and the
stylesheet apps/web imports come from the same release.
